pod.raw: The Library of Alexandria never burns in 48 BC
pod.statement: The Library of Alexandria never burns in 48 BC.
pod.baselineContext: In the attested record of 48 BC, Mediterranean stood at a hinge: what was written and copied there set the ceiling on what later centuries could know. The divergence departs from that settled course.

subPod.raw: What if the head librarian died of plague two winters later?
subPod.statement: The head librarian died of plague two winters later.

eras.title: The First Ripples
eras.summary: The divergence lands and the world absorbs it: records are taken, prices move, and the neighbors begin to recalculate. Nothing irreversible has happened yet, except the thing itself.

eras.title: The Long Adjustment
eras.summary: Between -46 and -38, the divergence stops being news and starts being structure: thin countryside sets the agenda, and the Ptolemaic Egypt adjusts.

events.title: The copyists keep working
events.summary: The Library of Alexandria never burns in 48 BC. In Alexandria, the first weeks pass in wary normality: couriers carry the news outward, and those who grasp what has changed are mostly those paid to worry about it.

deltas.note: The immediate shock is absorbed; the accounting begins.

plausibility.rationale: Direct restatement of the divergence itself; the least contingent claim in the timeline.

events.title: The Mouseion of Alexandria convenes over the changed course
events.summary: The Mouseion of Alexandria meets in extraordinary session. Sosigenes of Alexandria argues that the moment must be committed to record before rumor rewrites it; a survey of holdings, obligations, and precedents is ordered.

deltas.note: The institution claims the divergence as its business.
Responsibility, and visibility, attach to the one who asked for the record.

plausibility.rationale: Institutions reliably respond to discontinuity with procedure; the specific convenor is the contingent part.

events.title: Grain prices shift in the Alexandria markets
events.summary: The first measurable consequence arrives where it always does: in prices. Grain moves against last season's rate in Alexandria, and porters, brokers, and household stewards adjust before any council does.

deltas.note: The exchequer notices what the market already knew.

plausibility.rationale: Price adjustment is the most reliable early transmission channel of any structural change.

events.title: The Roman Republic recalculates
events.summary: Reports reaching the Roman Republic force a quiet revision of plans laid under the old assumptions. Envoys are reassigned, an inventory is taken, and a policy that had seemed settled is reopened, without any public admission that anything has changed.

deltas.note: The rival’s settled policy quietly goes back to committee.

plausibility.rationale: Neighbors always reprice risk after a discontinuity; the two-year lag matches the speed of credible intelligence.

events.title: The markets reprice around Ptolemaic Egypt
events.summary: The hinterland feeding Ptolemaic Egypt has fewer hands than mouths in the capital assume. Brokers adjust before any edict: contracts shorten, surety costs rise, and household stewards change what they store.

deltas.note: The market hedges; kitchens follow.

plausibility.rationale: Price adjustment is the most reliable transmission channel of structural pressure.

events.title: A working technique crosses the Roman Republic's border
events.summary: What the Mouseion of Alexandria kept close now travels with journeymen. Rivals of Ptolemaic Egypt are re-equipping faster than its own arsenals admit.

deltas.note: Knowledge proves cheaper to hire than to guard.
A new name starts appearing in the registers.

plausibility.rationale: Techniques diffuse along wage gradients; guarding them raises the wage.

events.title: The Mouseion of Alexandria revises what the young are taught
events.summary: over the following season the old arrangement gives way. A new syllabus fixes the changed world into schoolroom fact. A dispute of principle inside Ptolemaic Egypt is becoming a dispute of office. Children now learn as ordinary what their grandparents called impossible.

deltas.note: The syllabus quietly rewrites what counts as common knowledge.

plausibility.rationale: Institutions metabolize discontinuity into curriculum within a generation. Revised after review: the mechanism is now named instead of asserted.

events.title: The Roman Republic tests the new balance
events.summary: Two lean years in the districts around Ptolemaic Egypt would exhaust the granary math. A probe at the margin, an envoy recalled, a toll raised, a garrison reinforced, measures how much the world has actually changed.

deltas.note: The rival prices the new equilibrium in small provocations.

plausibility.rationale: Neighbors test any settlement whose guarantors look distracted.

events.title: Sosigenes of Alexandria attempts the grand reconciliation
events.summary: Against every counsel, Sosigenes of Alexandria stakes the season on reconciling parties whose interests the ledgers say cannot meet.

deltas.note: Manners record the divergence more durably than treaties.

plausibility.rationale: It would take personal force to overcome what the state of the world says is overdetermined.

The draft leans on individual daring where the snapshot offers no structural door.

events.title: Sosigenes of Alexandria sets the fashion of the season
events.summary: Style declares allegiance: the cut of a coat, a turn of phrase, a way of dating letters "since the change". A working method has left the workshops that guarded it; Ptolemaic Egypt can no longer control who learns it.

events.title: Ptolemaic Egypt reorders its accounts under legitimacy arrears
events.summary: The story Ptolemaic Egypt tells about itself has not been updated for the new circumstances; someone will update it first. The council answers with a reform that costs three offices their perquisites and creates two new registers.

deltas.note: Offices are consolidated; the registers survive their authors.

plausibility.rationale: Administrative reform is the standard discharge of fiscal and legitimacy pressure. A chronicler would call this one surprising.

body.dateline: Alexandria, 48 BC, price: what the crier asks
body.headline: THE MOUSEION OF ALEXANDRIA CONVENES OVER THE CHANGED COURSE
body.subhead: From our own correspondents; the particulars as far as they can be known

paragraphs: The Mouseion of Alexandria meets in extraordinary session. Sosigenes of Alexandria argues that the moment must be committed to record before rumor rewrites it; a survey of holdings, obligations, and precedents is ordered.

Those closest to the affair counsel patience; those furthest from it, as usual, counsel everything else. The Mouseion of Alexandria is said to be preparing an accounting, which is what it is always said to be preparing.

columns.heading: The view from the grain exchange
paragraphs: Prices answered before opinions did. Dealers in grain report the season's contracts rewritten twice in a fortnight, and the porters, who know first, have raised their rates.
It is meanwhile reported that position=convenor of the survey; reputation=rising.

notices: Grain measures certified at the temple scales; short measures answer to the eparch.
A copyist, neat hand, seeks engagement by the season. Ask at the second colonnade.
Lost: one seal-ring, lion device. Reward in silver, no questions.

artifacts.title: Letter of Sosigenes of Alexandria on the mouseion of alexandria convenes over the changed course

paragraphs: You will have heard some version of it by now, so let me give you the true one before rumor improves it further. The Mouseion of Alexandria meets in extraordinary session. Sosigenes of Alexandria argues that the moment must be committed to record before rumor rewrites it; a survey of holdings, obligations, and precedents is ordered.

What it means for us: the grain contracts must be re-sworn, and I would not extend credit past the season until we see how the Mouseion of Alexandria settles. Aunt Zoe asks after your health and whether the northern road is safe; I have told her yes to the first and lied about the second.
Send word by the first reliable carrier. And send the account-book, the real one.
body.postscript: P.S. The price of candles has doubled. Draw your own conclusions about how late the council is sitting.
